questions.prompt: In the `flex` shorthand, what is the order of the three values?

options.text: grow, shrink, basis
basis, grow, shrink
shrink, basis, grow
grow, basis, alignment

questions.explanation: The common three-value form is `flex: <grow> <shrink> <basis>`, for example `1 1 12rem`.

questions.prompt: Why is `margin-inline-start` often preferable to `margin-left` in reusable UI?

options.text: It always means the physical top margin
It follows the inline start edge in different writing directions
It sets both horizontal margins
It only works in grid containers

questions.explanation: Logical properties follow writing mode and direction; inline start is not always the physical left edge.

questions.prompt: Which statements about a three-value `flex` shorthand are correct?

options.text: The first value is flex-grow.
The second value is flex-shrink.
The third value is flex-basis.
The third value is `z-index`.

questions.explanation: The three-value shorthand order is grow, shrink, then basis.

questions.prompt: What happens to unoccupied repeated tracks with `auto-fit` when there are fewer items than tracks?

options.text: The browser inserts empty elements
The grid becomes a flex container
Empty tracks collapse so occupied tracks can expand
The tracks are always fixed at one pixel

questions.explanation: `auto-fit` collapses empty repeated tracks; this lets populated tracks expand within their sizing limits.

questions.prompt: Match each selector construct to its specificity behavior.
questions.explanation: `:where()` contributes zero; `:is()` takes its most specific argument; class and pseudo-class selectors each add class-column weight.

questions.prompt: What does `1fr` distribute in a grid track definition?

options.text: One root font-size unit
One viewport-width unit
One fraction of each item's intrinsic width
A share of the available free space after fixed sizing and gaps

questions.explanation: Flexible `fr` tracks divide available grid space after non-flexible sizing and gutters are accounted for.

questions.prompt: Why might a long URL force a flex or grid item wider than expected?

options.text: Its automatic minimum size can preserve min-content width
`gap` adds the URL length to the item
`z-index` prevents shrinking
`box-sizing` defaults to `border-box`

questions.explanation: Flex and grid items can retain a min-content-based automatic minimum; `min-width: 0` often permits the intended shrinkage.

questions.prompt: Select all correct statements about Grid's `auto-fit` card-wall pattern.

options.text: It requires JavaScript to count columns.
It can be combined with `repeat()`.
`minmax()` can set a minimum track size.
It can adapt without a width media query.

questions.explanation: Intrinsic grid sizing can create responsive columns without script-driven item counting.

questions.prompt: What does `clamp(1rem, 2vw, 2rem)` do?

options.text: Always returns exactly `2vw`
Uses a preferred fluid value constrained to a minimum and maximum
Chooses the smallest of three values
Changes only at a media-query breakpoint

questions.explanation: `clamp(min, preferred, max)` bounds a preferred value continuously rather than requiring a breakpoint.

questions.prompt: What must an ancestor do before descendants can respond to its inline size with a size container query?

options.text: Set `position: relative`
Set `display: flex`
Establish a query container, commonly with `container-type: inline-size`
Add an ID selector

questions.explanation: A size query needs an eligible ancestor query container; `container-type: inline-size` is a common opt-in.

questions.prompt: Match each responsive technique to what it measures.
questions.explanation: Media, container, and supports rules query different inputs.

questions.prompt: What does `:where(.menu, .toolbar)` contribute to selector specificity?

options.text: One ID
The specificity of the first matching selector
The specificity of every argument added together
Zero specificity

questions.explanation: The `:where()` pseudo-class and its selector list contribute zero specificity.

questions.prompt: What does `:is(.card, #featured)` contribute to specificity?

options.text: The specificity of its most specific argument, here the ID
Always zero
The sum of both arguments
Only the specificity of the element matched at runtime

questions.explanation: `:is()` takes the specificity of its most specific argument, independent of which argument matches.

questions.prompt: Which statements about CSS logical properties are correct?

options.text: They refer to inline or block directions.
They always mean left and right.
Their physical side can vary by writing mode.
`padding-inline` can set both inline sides.

questions.explanation: Logical properties follow writing mode and direction, so inline and block do not always map to horizontal and vertical.

questions.prompt: Which declaration normally wins between a normal declaration in a layer and a normal unlayered author declaration?

options.text: The layered declaration in every case
The unlayered declaration
Whichever selector has fewer classes
Whichever appears first

questions.explanation: For normal author declarations, unlayered declarations outrank declarations in named layers before specificity is compared.

questions.prompt: Match each declaration to its layout use.

columns.label: Permit a flex/grid item to shrink

questions.explanation: These declarations respectively distribute flexible grid space, change minimum sizing, and create gutters.

questions.prompt: Which style is a sensible mobile-first pattern?

options.text: Start with desktop-only styles and override every rule at each smaller size
Use only fixed pixel widths
Write the narrow base layout, then add `min-width` enhancements
Put every rule in a separate media query

questions.explanation: A mobile-first base makes the narrow layout the default and adds constraints for wider viewports.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `@supports (display: grid)`?

options.text: Load a stylesheet only on mobile
Increase selector specificity
Create a grid container automatically
Conditionally apply rules when the browser supports the tested feature

questions.explanation: `@supports` performs feature queries; it does not itself set the tested property.

questions.prompt: Which statements about cascade layers are correct for normal author declarations?

options.text: Declared layer order ranks layered declarations.
Unlayered normal declarations outrank layered normal declarations.
Every layered declaration outranks every unlayered declaration.
Specificity is compared after cascade priority.

questions.explanation: Layer priority is evaluated before specificity; for normal author styles, unlayered declarations outrank layered ones.

questions.prompt: Which rule is intended specifically for print output?

options.text: `@media print`
`@container print`
`@supports print`
`@layer print`

questions.explanation: The `print` media type targets paged output such as printing or print preview.

questions.prompt: When is a CSS transition a natural choice?

options.text: When a multi-step sequence must run without a state change
When a property should animate between values after a state change
When defining font files
When selecting a parent based on its children

questions.explanation: Transitions interpolate between before and after values when a change occurs; keyframes define multi-step animations.

questions.prompt: Match each CSS mechanism to a suitable use.
questions.explanation: Transitions animate state changes, keyframes define steps, and the media feature exposes a user preference.

questions.prompt: What is the role of `@keyframes`?

options.text: Define responsive breakpoints
Set the cascade layer order
Define named animation stages or property values over time
Register a custom HTML element

questions.explanation: `@keyframes` defines named animation steps that an animation can reference.

questions.prompt: What should a stylesheet do for users who request reduced motion?

options.text: Hide all interactive controls
Increase animation duration
Ignore the preference for decorative animations
Reduce or remove nonessential motion while preserving usable state changes

questions.explanation: Use `prefers-reduced-motion` to provide a less animated experience without removing essential information.

questions.prompt: Which conditions are valid uses for CSS feature or environment queries?

options.text: Use `@supports` to test a CSS feature.
Use `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` for a preference.
Use `@container` to query an eligible container.
Use `@supports` to test whether an HTML element exists.

questions.explanation: Feature, media-preference, and container queries answer different questions; `@supports` does not inspect document markup.

questions.prompt: What problem does `min-width: 0` commonly solve on a flex or grid child?

options.text: It allows the item to shrink below its automatic min-content minimum
It makes the item exactly zero pixels wide
It disables all intrinsic sizing
It prevents the item from wrapping

questions.explanation: A zero minimum width can let a flex/grid item shrink rather than overflow because of long or unbreakable content.

questions.prompt: Match each overflow symptom to a first CSS investigation.

rows.label: Long URL widens a grid item
Card breaks in a narrow slot

questions.explanation: Overflow and stacking bugs often originate in intrinsic minimums, container sizing, or stacking-context boundaries.

questions.prompt: What is the key distinction between a viewport media query and a container query?

options.text: Media queries test CSS classes; container queries test IDs
The media query tests the viewport/environment; a container query tests an eligible ancestor container
Container queries can only test color
They always measure the same box

questions.explanation: Viewport queries adapt to the page environment, while size container queries adapt a component to its container.

questions.prompt: Which technique is appropriate for an element aligned to the viewport while scrolling?

options.text: `position: static`
`display: inline`
`position: fixed`
`float: fixed`

questions.explanation: `position: fixed` typically positions relative to the viewport, subject to containing-block effects from certain ancestors.

questions.prompt: Which practices help avoid accidental overflow in responsive layouts?

options.text: Set `overflow: hidden` on the whole page without investigation.
Allow flex/grid text items to shrink with `min-width: 0` when appropriate.
Use `minmax(0, 1fr)` when a grid track must shrink below min-content.
Test long unbroken strings and code blocks.

questions.explanation: Address intrinsic sizing at the responsible item or track; blanket clipping can hide content and usability problems.

questions.prompt: What is the usual effect of `overflow: auto` on an element?

options.text: It always clips overflow without scrolling
It expands the element to fit all content
It removes the element from layout
It provides scrolling when the content overflows

questions.explanation: `overflow: auto` creates scrollable overflow when needed; exact scrollbar presentation is platform-dependent.

questions.prompt: Which property is the most direct choice to create space between flex items without adding outer margins?

options.text: `gap`
`outline`
`z-index`
`object-fit`

questions.explanation: The `gap` property controls gutters between flex items.

questions.prompt: Match each declaration to the behavior it controls.

columns.label: Fluid value with lower and upper limits
Show fallback text while a font loads

questions.explanation: These are common tools for fluid sizing, print styles, and resilient font loading.

questions.prompt: Why can a large `z-index` still fail to place a child above a neighboring component?

options.text: `z-index` is measured in pixels
The child is confined to its ancestor's stacking context
The child must always be a grid item
The cascade ignores integer values

questions.explanation: Stacking contexts are independent; descendants cannot outrank elements outside their context solely by using a larger number.

questions.prompt: Which statements about CSS custom properties are correct?

options.text: They are declared with names beginning `--`.
They are automatically compiled into Sass variables.
They can be read with `var()`.
Values can inherit through the element tree.

questions.explanation: Custom properties participate in the CSS cascade and inheritance; Sass variables are a separate build-time feature.

questions.prompt: Which state selector is the preferred direct hook for keyboard-visible focus styling?

options.text: `:visited`
`::marker`
`:focus-visible`
`:empty`

questions.explanation: `:focus-visible` targets focus when the browser determines a visible focus indication is appropriate.

questions.prompt: What does `var(--surface, white)` use when `--surface` is not defined or usable at computed-value time?

options.text: The initial value of every property
The parent element's background
The first declared color in the file
`white`

questions.explanation: The second argument is a fallback for an absent or invalid custom property at computed-value time.

questions.prompt: Which statements about transitions and keyframe animations are correct?

options.text: A transition usually needs a property value change to trigger.
Keyframes can describe multiple stages.
Transitions can define an arbitrary named sequence without keyframes.
Reduced-motion preferences should be considered for both.

questions.explanation: Transitions describe interpolation between changed values; keyframes define named stages.

questions.prompt: Why is an `@font-face` rule often paired with `font-display: swap`?

options.text: It allows fallback text to render while the web font loads
It forces the font file to load synchronously before HTML
It converts the font into a system font
It disables fallback fonts

questions.explanation: `swap` allows a fallback face to render immediately and swaps to the web font when available.

questions.prompt: Which declaration keeps a responsive image from exceeding its containing block's width?

options.text: `width: 100vw`
`max-width: 100%`
`min-width: 100%`
`overflow: visible`

questions.explanation: A maximum width of 100% prevents the image from exceeding its containing block while allowing smaller intrinsic size.

questions.prompt: Which practices improve keyboard and visual accessibility?

options.text: Provide a visible focus style.
Maintain adequate text/background contrast.
Respect user motion preferences.
Use color as the only indication of errors.

questions.explanation: Focus visibility, contrast, reduced motion, and non-color cues make interfaces more usable.

questions.prompt: What is the most reliable first step when a responsive component breaks only in a narrow sidebar?

options.text: Increase every `z-index`
Add a new global reset immediately
Inspect the component's available container width and its intrinsic minimum sizes
Set all descendants to `position: absolute`

questions.explanation: A component's container width and min-content constraints often explain failures that viewport breakpoints cannot.
